title: Day 2: Śrī Kṛṣṇa as the Sole Enjoyer
description: Authentic study of Principle 2 of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura: Realizing Śrī Kṛṣṇa as the only Puruṣa and shedding the enjoyer mentality in community.

questions.question: What is the exact philosophical formulation of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura's Principle 2?
options: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, is the only enjoyer. Everyone and everything else is the object of His enjoyment.
Devotional service should be free from all desire for fruitive gain and mental speculation.
One should be more tolerant than a tree and offer all respect to others.
Chanting the holy name is the only process to cross the material ocean.
questions.reference: Reflections on Sacred Teachings V, Principle 2
questions.explanation: Principle 2 states: 'The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, is the only enjoyer. Everyone and everything else is the object of His enjoyment.'

questions.question: Consider the relationship between community members and the Supreme Lord:
questions.assertion: Healthy communication and genuine cooperation can only flourish in a community when devotees cease viewing themselves as enjoyers.
questions.reason: When individuals operate in a 'salvationist consciousness,' they seek personal peace, self-preservation, and material accumulation rather than centering relationships on pleasing Kṛṣṇa.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.reference: Reflections on Sacred Teachings V, Principle 2
questions.explanation: His Holiness Bhakti Tirtha Swami Maharaja explains that pseudo-community arises when people come to devotee association asking 'what can I get?' rather than 'what can I give?' Only when Kṛṣṇa is recognized as the sole enjoyer (puruṣa) does genuine spiritual community emerge.

questions.question: According to Principle 2 and Bhagavad-gītā 15.7, the living entity (jīva) and the Supreme Lord (Kṛṣṇa) are identical in both quality and quantity.
questions.reference: Reflections on Sacred Teachings V, Principle 2 & BG 15.7
questions.explanation: The living entities are acintya-bhedābheda-tattva: qualitatively one with Kṛṣṇa as spirit, but quantitatively different as His eternal infinitesimal fragmental parts (mamaivāṁśo jīva-loke jīva-bhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ).

questions.question: In the commentary on Principle 2, what term is used to describe a community where members associate primarily to ensure their personal peace, happiness, and material accumulation?
options: Pseudo-community
Paramahaṁsa-maṭha
Daiva-varṇāśrama
Nitya-saṅga
questions.reference: Reflections on Sacred Teachings V, Principle 2
questions.explanation: The text explains that when people join a community to see what they can get out of the situation rather than what they can give, it becomes a 'pseudo-community' because it lacks true communication and selfless cooperation.

questions.question: What is the primary spiritual consequence when devotees in a community genuinely shift from an enjoyer mentality to recognizing Kṛṣṇa as the sole Puruṣa?
options: Ego-driven competition dissolves, giving rise to authentic communication, mutual respect, and selfless cooperation in service.
Devotees abandon all community responsibilities and retire to secluded caves.
Devotional rules are abandoned because everyone acts purely on personal whim.
Material opulence increases automatically without the need for any service.
questions.reference: Reflections on Sacred Teachings V, Principle 2
questions.explanation: When we recognize Kṛṣṇa as the only enjoyer and our godbrothers and godsisters as His beloved servants, possessiveness and friction vanish, creating a true spiritual family.

questions.question: Which of the following mindsets characterize a 'salvationist consciousness' as criticized in Principle 2? (Select all that apply)
options: Focusing primarily on self-preservation and personal peace
Seeking material accumulation under the umbrella of community
Evaluating devotee association based on 'what can I get?' rather than 'what can I give?'
Eagerly desiring to be the humble servant of the servant of the Lord
questions.reference: Reflections on Sacred Teachings V, Principle 2
questions.explanation: Salvationist consciousness centers around self-interest, self-preservation, and personal comfort, which directly obstructs pure unmotivated devotional surrender.

questions.question: Which Sanskrit term designates the Supreme Enjoyer (Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa) in contrast to all living entities who are prakṛti (the enjoyed)?
options: Puruṣa
Māyā
Guṇa
Karma
questions.reference: Reflections on Sacred Teachings V, Principle 2
questions.explanation: God alone is the Puruṣa (the Supreme Male / Supreme Enjoyer), while all souls and energies are prakṛti (the feminine / enjoyed potency meant for His satisfaction).

questions.question: Identify the FALSE statement regarding Principle 2 of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura:
options: A devotee should expect the temple community to cater to their personal comfort and validate their false ego.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the only enjoyer, and everyone else is an object of His enjoyment.
Deep spiritual relationships cannot exist if community members are primarily focused on self-preservation.
questions.reference: Reflections on Sacred Teachings V, Principle 2
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is false. Expecting others to cater to one's personal comfort is the manifestation of the enjoyer disease that Principle 2 seeks to uproot.

questions.question: Match each spiritual term from Principle 2 with its proper Vaiṣṇava understanding:
right: The Supreme Enjoyer — Śrī Kṛṣṇa alone
The enjoyed potency — all living beings
Driven by self-interest and 'what can I get'
Driven by selfless service and 'what can I give'
questions.reference: Reflections on Sacred Teachings V, Principle 2
questions.explanation: Principle 2 contrasts genuine community centered on Kṛṣṇa's pleasure with pseudo-community centered on personal exploitation.

questions.question: A devotee feels upset because someone else was selected to lead a prominent service they wanted. Applying Principle 2, how should this devotee process their feelings?
options: Remember that Kṛṣṇa is the only enjoyer and master of service; enthusiastically assist the devotee who was selected and find joy in Kṛṣṇa's pleasure.
Complain to everyone in the temple that management is biased and unfair.
Boycott the program and refuse to participate in any other seva.
Create a secret group to lobby for personal leadership in the next festival.
questions.reference: Reflections on Sacred Teachings V, Principle 2
questions.explanation: Since Kṛṣṇa is the only enjoyer, any service rendered by any devotee is for His satisfaction. Rejoicing in others' service is the genuine symptom of having internalized Principle 2.
